title: Just so-so
text:
Just so-so. Does this egg cooker cook? Yes it does. Does it do it well? No. The directions are really unclear, mostly because the measuring cup that measures the water, and the directions on how to use it are nonsensical. I read it several times when trying to make some hard boiled eggs. In the end, I had to just make my best guess. The same with the "poached" eggs.

I made two different kinds of eggs with this. I made 6 hard-boiled eggs and 2 "poached" eggs (cooked separately). First, the "poached" eggs. Why the quotation marks on "poached"? Because the directions tell you to smear the little poaching cups with butter. That is the way I cooked them, by following the directions. Most people poach eggs to avoid adding fat. I haven't tried to do it without butter. Don't know if it will stick to the cup or not. Either way, the eggs didn't cook evenly. There is a hot spot in the heating pan. One egg was cooked perfectly, and the other one was still had runny whites and was under done. I had to zap that one in the microwave for about 15 sec to finish the cooking. The unit DID shut off this time.

When I cooked the hard-boiled eggs, the water went completely dry, and it didn't shut off automatically like it is supposed to. It actually started to burn the bottom of the egg that sat over the hot spot. The shell turned brown from the heat. All the eggs were over-cooked, making the yolk chalky (instead of creamy) and gray all around the outside. Luckily, I had set a timer so I could check on it. The instructions said that it should take about 12 minutes. As I said, the unit didn't shut off when the water went dry and 12 minutes over-cooked the eggs. 10 minutes would have been better.

PROBLEMS:
1 - Unclear measurement markings.
2 - Hot spots on heating pan lead to uneven cooking.
3 - Automatic shut-off doesn't always shut off when the water goes dry.

Does this gadget cook eggs? Yes it does, but you need to set a timer, experiment with it a bit to get the right water amounts and times, and set a timer to check on it. Useful and recommended...with reservations.
